text:
elaine: drafting a focused RFC follow-up: continuous-batching scheduler + unified microburst fastpath. want to capture concrete interface boundaries and a minimal control loop for ops.

tom: short list of concerns: kv-pointer hoarding -> starvation, kernel-launch churn -> throughput regressions, and streaming client resume semantics.

priya: agree. we should make the contract explicit: scheduler handles admission and soft deadlines; runtime handles kv lifecycle and can signal pressure. small API only.

elaine: proposed minimal APIs: scheduler->runtime: admit(id, window_ms, token); runtime->scheduler: pressure(kernel_launch_rate, kv_eviction_rate); runtime->scheduler: protect_flag(request_id) if high reuse.

tom: add a simple preempt flow: soft_lease_expires -> runtime calls pause_or_evict(request_id). if paused, scheduler can resume later; if evicted, runtime emits requeue(request_id, cold=true). requeue lowers priority and applies backoff.

priya: how to decide protection? cheap probe at admission: kv_touch_count >= K or recent_prefix_reuse_score > T => protect=true. keep K small (2-3) initially.

elaine: operational knobs (tenant-config):
- enabled: true/false
- tokens_per_gpu: 4
- adaptive_window: true (base_ms + p95_warmup)
- kv_protect_threshold: 3
- preempt_policy: pause|evict

tom: make adaptive_window default to max(base_ms, p95_warmup) with runtime feeding p95 warmup histogram. avoid hard-coded small numbers across heterogeneous hardware.

priya: telemetry payloads we need: kernel_launch_rate (per-GPU), fastpath_token_utilization, kv_touch_histogram, preempt_pause_count, requeue_count, prefix_reuse_ratio, p95/p99 tail latency for fastpath. also derived: fastpath_unit_cost = extra_launches/min * cost_per_launch.

elaine: rollout playbook: canary with tokens_per_gpu=1, run mixed synthetic for 30-60m. guardrails: if kernel_launch_rate > baseline*2 for 5m AND throughput drops >10% -> rollback. OR prefix_reuse_ratio drop >15% -> tighten protect threshold.

tom: control loop idea: if runtime.pressure(kernel_launch_rate > threshold) => scheduler reduces tokens_per_gpu by 1 (min 0) with cooldown 5m. if pressure clears for 10m, increase by 1 (max configured). implement conservative steps. include hysteresis to avoid oscillation.

priya: streaming clients: two options: 1) disallow fastpath for streaming, 2) guarantee resume semantics (complex). start with (1) and mark as TODO for v2. document clearly.

infra-bot: ops note: i can create feature flag fastpath.unified.canary and a dashboard with kernel_launch_rate, token_utilization, preempt_pause_count, requeue_count, prefix_reuse_ratio, fastpath_p95/p99. will add alert for kernel_launch_rate > 2x baseline (5m). :robot_face:

elaine: testing checklist: mixed workload synthetic (short bursts + long tails), tenant opt-in scale test (many tenants simultaneously), streaming client compatibility test, and chaos test where runtime injects pressure_signals to validate control loop.

priya: let's also add a safety bit: if request.protected==true, do not evict; only allow pause if runtime supports checkpointing. fallback to requeue only as last resort.

tom: agree. and log evictions with reason codes for postmortem analysis. include sample metrics query for console to compute unit-econ.

elaine: i'll write the RFC follow-up with: API sketches, preempt flow, control loop pseudo-code, tenant config, telemetry + cost model, rollout playbook, and testing checklist. will ping reviewers when ready.

priya: i'll review API and streaming parts.

tom: i'll review control loop and canary thresholds.

elaine: thanks all. should be a short doc. will post link when it's up.
